tasks.title: Public parks priorities
tasks.instruction: You must answer this question. Write 220–260 words in an appropriate style.

promptBlocks.text: Your class has listened to a radio discussion about how local authorities should balance making public parks convenient for visitors with ensuring long-term environmental and financial responsibility. You have made the notes below.

promptBlocks.heading: Priorities for public parks
listItems: installing more lighting and seating for evening use
introducing a small entry fee for non-residents
creating dedicated wildlife zones with restricted access

paragraphs: Better lighting and benches would make parks usable after dark, which is great for people who work late. But it might disturb wildlife and increase maintenance costs.
A small fee for visitors from outside the area could raise money for upkeep. However, it might discourage people from using the park and feel unfair.
Wildlife zones would protect biodiversity, but closing off parts of the park could annoy regular users who want to walk their dogs or play sports.

promptBlocks.text: Write an essay for your tutor discussing two of the priorities in your notes. You should explain which priority you think is more important for balancing access and long-term responsibility in public parks, giving reasons in support of your answer. You may, if you wish, make use of the opinions expressed in the discussion, but you should use your own words as far as possible.

tasks.title: Proposal for park volunteer scheme
tasks.instruction: Answer one of the following questions (2–4). Write 220–260 words in an appropriate style.

promptBlocks.text: Your local council is planning to introduce a volunteer scheme to help maintain public parks while keeping them accessible to all. The council's parks manager has invited proposals from community groups for how this scheme should operate.

Write a proposal for the parks manager. In your proposal, you should:

• recommend two specific tasks that volunteers could carry out
• explain how the scheme could attract and retain volunteers from different age groups
• suggest how the council could ensure the scheme does not reduce its own long-term responsibility for park maintenance

tasks.title: Email about park event restrictions
tasks.instruction: Answer one of the following questions (2–4). Write 220–260 words in an appropriate style.

promptBlocks.text: You are a member of a local park users' group. The programme coordinator of the council's public realm strategy has emailed your group about a proposal to ban all commercial events (such as food festivals and charity runs) from the main city park to reduce wear and tear. Some group members support the ban, while others argue it will make the park less vibrant and reduce funding for maintenance.

Write an email to the programme coordinator. In your email, you should:

• explain your position on the proposed ban
• analyse one potential implication for the local community if the ban goes ahead
• propose an alternative action that could protect the park while still allowing some events

tasks.title: Review of a park restoration project
tasks.instruction: Answer one of the following questions (2–4). Write 220–260 words in an appropriate style.

promptBlocks.heading: Reviews wanted: Park restoration projects
paragraphs: Have you visited a public park that has recently undergone a restoration or redesign aimed at balancing visitor access with environmental care?
We want to hear about your experience. Write a review for our local lifestyle website.

Describe the changes made to the park. Evaluate how well the project balanced making the park more convenient for people with protecting it for the long term. Would you recommend this approach to other parks? Why or why not?
The best reviews will be published on our website.
